summary: A 40-section extraction and architectural reinterpretation of Timothy Williamson's Knowledge and Its Limits, applying all prior lenses (Zero, Ganesha/Leonardo/Krishna/Shani, Topological, Statistical, Causal, Searle, Floridi, Dretske, Fagin, Gardenfors, Pramana) to conclude that KnowledgeOS must stop trying to define knowledge reductively and instead preserve knowledge attributions, factivity, broadness, primeness, anti-luminosity, margins, and evidence/assertion distinctions.
contribution_assessment: Major synthesis document: derives 7 new Kernel invariants (K-INV-01..07), corrects three earlier proposals (capacity=knowledge, Agent->projection->Knowledge Space direction, knowledge->language chain), reinterprets the S_t snapshot formula as a projection not the knowledge itself, proposes a Q(K,P,C,t) quantifiable-properties tuple and a knowledge-margin M(P,A,C), and produces a full Kernel inside/outside/above-boundary list plus a final KnowledgeOS definition and meta-model diagram.

summary: A 38-section extraction of Brandom's Making It Explicit, proposing commitment (not fact) as the key primitive, deontic scorekeeping, a commitment-and-relation Kernel substrate, an Inferential Content Principle and Explicitness Principle, and K_t^A=(P,C,E,I,N,R) as a candidate dynamic Knowledge Space state formalization; explicitly placed eighth in the McGinn/Floridi/Dretske/Fagin/Gardenfors/Searle/Williamson/Brandom research arc.
contribution_assessment: Major synthesis: introduces commitment/entitlement primitives, revises the Kernel candidate list to a commitment-and-relation substrate, adds an inferential boundary type, distinguishes five inference regimes, and warns against literalizing Brandom's scorekeeping theory as the Kernel itself (repeating an earlier Fagin mistake).

summary: A 50-section extraction of Gelfond & Kahl's knowledge-representation/ASP textbook, explicitly framed as a major refinement of the whole KnowledgeOS model rather than another lens: introduces computable interpretations of the knowledge-state snapshot, nonmonotonic default reasoning, dynamic-domain state transitions, elaboration tolerance, open/closed-world distinctions, 8 new invariants (K-INV-08..15), an Epistemic Model Separation Principle, and three final boxed definitions of Knowledge, Knowledge Space, and the KnowledgeOS Kernel.
contribution_assessment: Very large synthesis: revises the Kernel candidate list into core-preservation vs derived-epistemic-machinery, adds K_t^A=Project(H≤t,D,R,A) and H_t->K_t^R formalizations, distinguishes historical/derivation/current-projection preservation as a major Kernel principle, and proposes final working definitions of Knowledge, Knowledge Space, and the Kernel.

summary: A governance/adjudication-process document reframing constitutional question C-15 (retraction) via a Knowledge Space + time-indexed Projection model, then critically reviewing a proposed Epistemic-state + Lifecycle-state split (naming it C-15-H1), raising four challenges (unestablished lifecycle-model claim, premature four-state architecture, unresolved lifecycle-ownership question, truth-vs-reliance conflation), and recommending it remain a research hypothesis pending formal HPA adjudication.
contribution_assessment: Substantial governance-methodology content: distinguishes brainstorming from formal Kernel-boundary work, proposes a Conceptual Model Inventory and a three-artifact (Current Law/Brainstorming Model/Falsification Matrix) governance process, and produces a detailed verdict table on a reviewed lifecycle-state proposal.
